tools.name: lingohub_list_projects
tools.description: List every Lingohub project this API key can see (owned and shared, across workspaces). Each entry has the title, its links and the workspace_url + project_url slugs that every other tool needs. GET /v1/projects.

tools.name: lingohub_get_project
tools.description: One project: title, description, owner email, configured locales (project_locales), timestamps and links. GET /v1/{workspace_url}/projects/{project_url}.

tools.name: lingohub_get_project_status
tools.description: Translation status of one project: each resource file with per-locale segment counts (NOT_TRANSLATED, DRAFT, TRANSLATED, APPROVED, ...), failing quality checks, the export formats it supports and whether a Git repository is connected and can be pushed to. GET .../projects/{project_url}/status.

tools.name: lingohub_get_workspace_status
tools.description: Translation progress of every project in one workspace: title, app URL, total segment count and per-locale counts by status (NOT_TRANSLATED, DRAFT, TRANSLATED, PREFILLED, APPROVED). GET /v1/{workspace_url}/projects/status.

tools.name: lingohub_create_project
tools.description: WRITE: create a new localization project in a workspace (needs settings-management permission on the key). Returns the new project with its links. It adds a project and changes nothing existing; repeating the call can create a second project. POST /v1/{workspace_url}/projects.

tools.name: lingohub_list_resources
tools.description: List a project's resource files: name, locale and links (including a download link). GET .../projects/{project_url}/resources.

tools.name: lingohub_download_resource
tools.description: Download one resource file as text, in one language. file_name is the file name as list_resources shows it (the folder goes in `path`). Long files are cut at 40000 characters (truncated: true); use request_export for a full copy. GET .../projects/{project_url}/resources/{file_name}.

tools.name: lingohub_upload_resource_file
tools.description: WRITE: upload one text resource file (JSON, properties, XLIFF, PO, ...) into a project. The language comes from the file name or from `language`. The import flags decide whether existing segments are changed or deactivated: with updating or deactivation on, translations already in Lingohub can be ov

tools.name: lingohub_delete_resource
tools.description: WRITE, DESTRUCTIVE: delete a resource container: the source-language file AND all its target-language files with their translations. file_name and path must address the source-language file. This cannot be undone through the API. Never retried. DELETE .../projects/{project_url}/resources/{file_name}

tools.name: lingohub_request_export
tools.description: Start an asynchronous export of a project's resource files as a ZIP. It creates an export job and changes no project data. Returns the export id; poll get_export until its status is SUCCESS to get the download URL. Without filters it exports every file and language. POST .../projects/{project_url}/e

tools.name: lingohub_get_export
tools.description: Status of an export started with request_export: overall and per-file status (NEW, SCHEDULED, PROCESSING, SUCCESS, SKIPPED, ERROR), error details and, when done, the pre-signed download URL of the ZIP. GET .../projects/{project_url}/exports/{export_id}.

tools.name: lingohub_list_context_images
tools.description: List the context images (screenshots that show translators where a text is used) of a project, with connected-segment counts and processing status. Paginated; page is zero-based. GET .../projects/{project_url}/contextImages.

tools.name: lingohub_delete_context_image
tools.description: WRITE, DESTRUCTIVE: delete one context image and its connections to text segments. Never retried. DELETE .../projects/{project_url}/contextImages/{image_id}.

tools.name: lingohub_push_to_repository
tools.description: WRITE: push the project's resource files to its linked Git repository (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket or Azure DevOps; the connection must already exist). Depending on push_type this commits to a branch or opens a pull request, so it changes the user's repository. Never retried. POST .../projects/{projec

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: lingohub_get_project, lingohub_get_workspace_status, lingohub_request_export, lingohub_get_export · Private data: lingohub_list_projects, lingohub_get_project_status, lingohub_list_resources, lingohub_download_resource, lingohub_upload_resource_file, lingohub_delete_resource, lingohub_request_export, lingohub_get_export, lingohub_push_to_repository · Public sink: lingohub_get_project, lingohub_create_project, lingohub_upload_resource_file, lingohub_request_export, lingohub_push_to_repository · Destructive: lingohub_delete_resource, lingohub_delete_context_image.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: lingohub_get_project, lingohub_get_workspace_status, lingohub_request_export, lingohub_get_export · Private data: lingohub_list_projects, lingohub_get_project_status, lingohub_list_resources, lingohub_download_resource, lingohub_upload_resource_file, lingohub_delete_resource, lingohub_request_export, lingohub_get_export, lingohub_push_to_repository · Public sink: lingohub_get_project, lingohub_create_project, lingohub_upload_resource_file, lingohub_request_export, lingohub_push_to_repository · Destructive: lingohub_delete_resource, lingohub_delete_context_image

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
